newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS - Australia's ABARE sees falling wheat prices.
newsitem.headline: RTRS - Australia's ABARE sees falling wheat prices.

text.p: The Australian Bureau of Agricultural and Resource Economics (ABARE) has maintained its forecast of the 1996/97 Australian wheat crop at 18.8 million tonnes and is forecasting falling world wheat prices in 1996/97.

The outlook for wheat prices had deteriorated since June, reflecting larger than expected wheat supplies in major exporting countries and downward revised forecasts of world import demand in 1996/97, ABARE, the Australian government's key commodity forecaster, said in its September outlook.

ABARE's forecast of an 18.8 million tonne crop for Australian wheat in 1996/97 (to June 30) is steady with its September Australian crop report forecast and would produce a crop 10.8 percent higher than 1995/96 production.
Domestic Australian wheat consumption is forecast to decline slightly in 1996/97 as a result of continued subdued demand from beef feedlots, ABARE said.
ABARE said Australian wheat export prospects received a boost from the Australian Wheat Board (AWB) negotiating wheat sales of about 100,000 tonnes a month to Iraq.
However, renewed international tensions surrounding Iraq in early September put these sales in doubt, it said.
Total Australian wheat exports are forecast at 12.92 million tonnes in 1996/97, almost steady with 12.05 million tonnes the year before.
ABARE forecasts the pool return for Australian Standard White will fall by 16.7 percent to A$210.00 a tonne in 1996/97.
World wheat prices are expected to stabilise after falling by US$85 a tonne from their peak in May to US$195 a tonne in early August, ABARE said.
They are then expected to increase marginally in coming months as stocks remain at relatively low levels, it said.
The world indicator price for wheat is forecast to average US$190 a tonne in 1996/97, down from $215.00 a tonne in 1995/96.
